To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a simple technique for sensing catechol-containing biomolecules by monitoring the absorbance change due to the surface charge-transfer (CT)-complex formation between catechol and the TiO2 surface.

the catechol adsorption on TiO2 induces a strong absorption band in the whole visible range, which is attributed to the charge-transfer complex formation between catechol and TiO2, and the time course of the adsorption can be traced by measuring the intensity change of the absorption band.
catechol can be detected on TiO2 via the formation of surface CT complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
surface chemistry and electrochemical properties of titanium(IV)oxide.
the surface charge-transfer complex formation and the application of the complex to biosensing.
the adsorption of a biomolecule, catechol, on a metal oxide semiconductor surface, TiO2, and the application of the adsorption process for the detection of the biomolecule.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
catechol adsorbs on the surface of TiO2 via the chelate formation with the surface Ti ions to induce the CT absorption, and the CT absorption is a useful indicator for the adsorption.

the adsorption of the catechols on the TiO2 particles induces the CT absorption band in the whole visible range, which can be used as a new sensing method for biomolecules bearing the phenolic hydroxy group.
the adsorption of 2-hydoxyphenol on TiO2 is accompanied with the formation of the CT complex, and the adsorption process is described by the Langmuir-type model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CT band of surface charge-transfer complex of catechol can be used for a new sensing technique for the catechol-containing biomolecules.
a new type of surface CT complex of a biomolecule with a semiconductor is formed on the semiconductor surface.
the adsorbed catechol on TiO2 can be used as a new sensing material for the catechol-containing molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the adsorption of the catechols on TiO2 surface induces a strong absorption of the visible light due to the CT from the HOMOs of catechol molecules to the conduction bands of TiO2 particles, and the absorption intensity depends on the adsorption amount of catechol.
the catechol molecule can be used as a simple and sensitive probe for detecting the presence of TiO2 particles.
catechol can be used as a model molecule to understand the interaction between biomolecules and TiO2.
